reason: The kill arm has landed: a melee blow that takes a monster's last hit point now runs mon.c killed() (3469-3473) and xkilled() (3476-3740) with mondead(), m_detach(), mon_leaving_level(), lifesaved_monster(), corpse_chance(), make_corpse(), exper.c experience() and attrib.c adjalign() beneath them, and the turn finishes. What keeps this at implementation is not a gap in the boundary below but the checklist gate's own circularity, recorded as a proposal at dc31f03: prepare --readiness requires the range head to equal HEAD and validateChecklist requires commitChecked to equal the range head, so a checklist can never name the commit that contains it. commitChecked below is therefore the pre-slice head, and every entry is already at a terminal status.

boundary.startingEvent: a movement keystroke whose destination square holds a hostile monster, and whose blow at uhitm.c hmon_hitmon():1847 takes the target's last hit point
boundary.endingEvent: the screen and cursor at the end of that turn, with the target off the map and its corpse, dropped inventory and treasure drop resolved
boundary.validInputs: the eight movement keys and their run and rush forms, with any role, race, gender and alignment; no F force-fight prefix, no ranged attack and no #twoweapon
boundary.observables: the random-number log, the full 24x80 screen with attributes, the cursor, and the persisted level.monsters grid, level.monlist chain, iflags.purge_monsters, the object pile on the target's square, svm.mvitals[].died, u.uexp, u.urexp, u.ualign.record, u.uluck and u.uconduct.killer
boundary.exclusions: the second two-weapon attack at hitum():791-812, which is the goal's next slice; force-fight, ranged and applied hits; a polymorphed hero via hmonas(); hero death at js/hack.js losehp()'s u.uhp < 1 branch; monster retaliation via mhitu.c mattacku(); pet-versus-monster melee via mhitm.c mattackm(); and steal.c mdrop_obj()'s equipped-object arm, which a monster that dies wearing or wielding something reaches and which is recorded as the deferral dead-monster-drops-equipped-gear

candidateListMethod.upstreamEntryPoints: mon.c killed() 3469-3473 and xkilled() 3476-3740, entered from uhitm.c hmon_hitmon():1904-1910. Every function xkilled() names was read in full: mondead() 3080-3177, monstone() 3286-..., m_detach() 2733-2803, mon_leaving_level() 2695-2730, unstuck() 3437-3467, mlifesaver() 2825-2836, lifesaved_monster() 2838-2884, vamprises() 2886-..., logdeadmon() 2996-3076, corpse_chance() 3180-3249, make_corpse() 563-941, zombie_maker() 361-380, zombie_form() 385-410, mongone() 3266-3283, and the macros LEVEL_SPECIFIC_NOCORPSE() 44-47 and KEEPTRAITS() 549-556. Beneath them: exper.c experience() 84-166, more_experienced() 168-203 and newexplevel() 298-304; attrib.c adjalign() 1297-1316 and change_luck(); steal.c relobj() 873-899 and mdrop_obj() 812-846; invent.c delobj() 1428-1433 and delobj_core() 1435-1462; zap.c obj_resists() 1458-1473; mkobj.c mkcorpstat(), mkobj() and place_object(); do.c flooreffects(); do_name.c safe_oname() 94-100.
candidateListMethod.dispatchTablesAndCatalogs: make_corpse()'s species switch at 581-748, transcribed group by group against the C rather than summarized, with the 154-line PM_ roster at 686-844 excluded because include/patchlevel.h:33 sets NH_DEVEL_STATUS to NH_STATUS_RELEASED and its `#else default:` at 846 is what compiles; xkilled()'s alignment if-chain at 3677-3722; corpse_chance()'s NATTK attack scan at 3200-3232; experience()'s two NATTK loops at 101-127; the four XKILL_ flags at hack.h:1368-1371; the CORPSTAT_ flags at hack.h:1189-1200.
candidateListMethod.reachableHelpers: Each helper was traced from xkilled() outward and its guard read before its body, so a refusal could be placed above the first draw, message or object on its path rather than after it. The random-number order was then confirmed twice: against a live replay of seed0200 and seed0006, and against nineteen fresh C recordings by scripts/run-hostile-melee-kill.mjs. The whole kill draws exactly rn2(6) then rn2(tmp) on the ordinary path; mondead()'s own two calls are species-gated to a steam vortex and a Keystone Kop and both stop.
candidateListMethod.javascriptCrossCheck: Before porting, `grep -rnE '\b(mondead|monDead|m_detach|mDetach|mon_leaving_level|monLeavingLevel|lifesaved_monster|lifesavedMonster|corpse_chance|corpseChance|make_corpse|makeCorpse|logdeadmon|adjalign|adjAlign|newexplevel|newExplevel)\b' js/` returned mondead 0, m_detach 2 (both comments), mon_leaving_level 4 (all comments), lifesaved_monster 0, corpse_chance 0, make_corpse 0, logdeadmon 0, adjalign 5 (all comments), and newexplevel 8 (a working port). `experience` returned 39 hits, none of them exper.c's function. Four predicates already existed under a second spelling and were converged rather than copied again: alwaysHostile and alwaysPeaceful (js/makemon.js, 3 hits), uniqueCorpstat (js/monmove.js, 3), zombieMaker (js/monmove.js, 3) and emitsLight (js/makemon_create.js, 5). `grep -rn 'heroIsBlind' js/` returns 11 separate copies; the slice reused js/startup_a11y.js's rather than adding a twelfth.
candidateListMethod.remainingLimits: Three things inside the boundary are pinned by unit test alone because no first-level fresh case reaches them: experience()'s AD_DRLI, extra_nasty(), level-above-8 and eel arms, which need species that do not generate on D:1; mondead()'s werejackal and chameleon reversion; and the svm.mvitals[].died cap at 255. make_corpse()'s twelve special-species groups are refused rather than ported, so a dragon, unicorn, long worm, vampire, mummy, zombie, golem or pudding that dies where corpse_chance() said yes stops; the Monk scan hit that on 3 of 59 adjacent seeds, all of them zombies.

sourceReview: Every branch and helper reachable from uhitm.c hmon_hitmon():1904 through the end of the turn was traced against the C source, with the first and last line of each cited span printed rather than inherited from a neighbouring comment. The call and random-number order was verified twice, once against a live replay of the two witness sessions and once against nineteen fresh C recordings. Every refusal's position was checked against the first draw, message or object on its path, and every refusal's condition against C's own guard; the treasure drop's rn2(6) is made unconditionally for exactly that reason, even though no witness rolls a zero. Two stubs remain inside the boundary and both are named above: make_corpse()'s twelve special species groups, and steal.c mdrop_obj()'s equipped-object arm. Three predicates that existed twice in js/ were converged rather than copied a third time, and js/startup_a11y.js canSeeMonster() and canSpotMonster() lost an `mhp < 1` guard that display.h's macros do not have and that made xkilled():3508 name a freshly killed monster 'it'.
